parsed.chain: Houston < Scots surname from Hugh + -ston; Hugh from Old French Hue, from Germanic *hug- ‘mind, spirit’ + ston/stone = settlement
parsed.reading: A stone-settlement of spirit or mind: a place founded on thought, will, or inner breath.
parsed.source: Oxford Dictionary of Family Names in Britain and Ireland; Online Etymology Dictionary

parsed.chain: hou + ston; hou ~ who/how; ston ~ stone/stand; who + stone = the one who stands firm
parsed.reading: The question of identity becomes a stone: who stands, who endures.

parsed.chain: houston ~ houst-on; fr. houst(e) ~ huste/huste? + on = one/on; sound suggests ‘on’ as impersonal agent
parsed.reading: An impersonal force acts: ‘one does,’ ‘it happens,’ without a named doer.

parsed.chain: houston ~ hûs-ton; ger./dial. Haus + ton; house + tone = the tone of the house
parsed.reading: The house speaks by its tone; dwelling becomes voice, atmosphere, and disposition.

parsed.chain: HOUSTON -> H + OUT + SON / or H + OUST + ON; out/oust + son = expelled offspring
parsed.reading: The son is cast out, or the inner heir is driven beyond the threshold.

parsed.chain: H O U S T O N -> Hidden Oracle Under Stone, The One Named
parsed.reading: A concealed oracle lies beneath stone: the named thing is a cover for hidden speech.

parsed.chain: H = the ladder/bridge; O = enclosure; U = vessel; S = serpent; T = cross; O = circle; N = descent/angle
